properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 is exposed as a selectable hash function in the Ivy playground (runtime dispatch at data.tsx:314: case "sha1" → crypto.sha1(childData)) and used in shipped Ivy DSL contract templates (RevealCollision collision-bounty demo at predefined.ts:59, HashOperations test at :250/:256, negative compile-error tests at :359/:366). These compile to Bitcoin Script OP_SHA1. The predefined.ts occurrences are demo/test contract strings; the data.tsx site is live application code users can trigger. Changeab

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Bitcoin ECDSA over secp256k1: ivy-bitcoin re-exports the curve module as its crypto layer (crypto.ts:7, export const secp256k1 = crypto.secp256k1) and signs transaction sighashes with secp256k1.signDER (spend.ts:113); the playground parses DER signatures back with fromDER (data.tsx:167). The curve is fixed by Bitcoin consensus rules — observable here, replaceable only by a Bitcoin protocol change (soft fork / new signature opcode), not by this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.7.5 is a dev-toolchain dependency: required by selfsigned@1.10.4 (lockfile:6172), which webpack-dev-server requires (lockfile:8193), to generate the local dev server's self-signed HTTPS certificate. node-forge's RSA is exposed there (dev-server cert keygen); no application call site in ivy-playground/ivy-bitcoin source. Shipped in the dev dependency graph only — changeable here by upgrading/removing the dev-server HTTPS path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES ships inside node-forge@0.7.5 (same chain as the RSA object: webpack-dev-server → selfsigned@1.10.4 → node-forge), where it supports the self-signed cert/keystore machinery. Dev-toolchain exposure only; no application call site. Available in the shipped library; no call site found in the application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge is the crypto library behind the playground's dev-server HTTPS: webpack-dev-server (lockfile:8193) → selfsigned@1.10.4 (:6167) → node-forge@0.7.5 (:4503, required at :6172). Its RSA/ASN.1/X.509 code generates the self-signed dev certificate. Dev toolchain, not shipped in the client bundle; changeable here by upgrading the chain (node-forge 0.7.5 is ancient — pre-2018).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 provides the pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations behind crypto-browserify's create-hash/create-hmac and pbkdf2 — i.e. it is the hash engine of the polyfill webpack bundles into the playground production client when ivy-bitcoin/bcrypto import Node's crypto. Old version (2.4.11, 2018) predates any hardening; no first-party call site, reachable only through the polyfill. Available in the shipped library; no call site found in the application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned@1.10.4 (lockfile entry :6167) is required by webpack-dev-server (:8193) to create the self-signed X.509 certificate for the local HTTPS dev server; it drives node-forge's RSA/ASN.1 internally. Dev-toolchain asset; its posture (self-signed dev cert, RSA keys) is observable here and changeable by upgrading the chain — selfsigned 1.10.4 uses node-forge 0.7.5-era defaults.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 (MD5/SHA-1/SHA-2/RIPEMD-160 pure-JS) is required by elliptic@6.x — the ECDSA/ECDH engine of the browserify-sign/create-ecdh chain inside crypto-browserify — so it ships in the webpack production client bundle beneath ivy-bitcoin/bcrypto's Node-crypto imports. Available in the shipped library; no direct first-party call site. Changeable by upgrading the polyfill chain.
